skills.name: Resume-JD Optimizer
skills.description: Generates a tailored two-page resume and matching cover letter from a job description and the candidate's per-track master resumes, in a plain human-written style, enforced by blocking build gates.
skills.author: Resume Generator Team

inputs.name: slug
inputs.description: Run slug passed as the skill's argument, e.g. /resume-jd-optimizer hiringcafe. Namespaces the posting and the data logs so concurrent sessions in one checkout do not collide. Never derived from the directory, branch or worktree. If omitted and exactly one input/jd-*.txt exists, its slug is inferred and reported

inputs.name: jd_path
inputs.description: Path to the job description, resolved from the slug. Missing is the only condition that halts a run; there is no input/jd.txt fallback

inputs.name: track_map
inputs.description: JSON map from JD text to track files. Its 'tracks' object is authoritative for which master-resume-{track}.md files exist. Read in the same batch as the JD at Step 2 and applied at Step 3: no_fit check, then title match for the primary, then keyword scoring for the secondary. Matching is on word boundaries, never bare substring

inputs.name: track_resume_paths
inputs.description: Per-track master resumes, selected from the JD role responsibilities. Each holds only what varies by track: Section 1 skills, then certificates, open source and behavioural examples written specifically for that kind of role. Facts live in input/profile.md and projects in input/projects.md, so a track file is no longer a complete record on its own. Skills come from every selected track, unioned; certificates and behavioural material from the primary. input/master-resume-bone.md is the anonymised sharing template and is never a source

inputs.name: profile
inputs.description: Shared, single-source record of every hard fact: employers, titles, dates, locations, company descriptions, education, and contact values. Not per-track and never duplicated into a track file, so two files cannot disagree about a fact. Read at Step 4 with the selected tracks. The frozen-facts gate reads it and refuses to run without it

inputs.name: projects
inputs.description: Shared project and product library: one entry per project with Company, Period, Tracks, Skills used, Measured results and a prose description. Not per-track and never duplicated into a track file. Read at Step 4 with the selected tracks. Supplies every experience bullet and every metric: a skill absent from all Skills used lines has no project evidence and may appear only in Technical Skills

inputs.name: output_dir
inputs.description: Output directory for the generated files (default: output/{YYYYMMDD})

outputs.name: tailored_resume
outputs.description: Markdown resume conforming to the output contract in scripts/convert_resume.py

outputs.name: cover_letter
outputs.description: Matching cover letter, generated from the finished resume

outputs.name: optimization_summary
outputs.description: Chat-only report: tracks selected, keyword coverage, requirements deliberately not claimed, entries omitted for missing detail, and the data/ files written

outputs.name: new_skills_log
outputs.description: JD skills with no match in any track file, grouped by track and appended for later review. Written instead of asking the user

outputs.name: master_resume_gaps_log
outputs.description: Anything that made the run weaker than it should have been: unmet must-haves, missing metrics, thin track files, drift between two track files. Grouped by track and appended

features: Track Map Lookup (title fast path, then keyword scoring)
Single-Source Shared Profile (facts split from per-track skills)
Shared Project Library with Per-Project Skill Evidence
ATS Keyword Coverage (JD skills absent from the record are absorbed into Technical Skills rows, listed and never claimed)
Blocking Quality Gates (scripts/verify_resume.py), including the claim-boundary gate
phases: Step 5: Generate Resume and Cover Letter

success_metrics.length: Two pages, roughly 900 words, never above 1050
success_metrics.gates: All six gates in scripts/verify_resume.py pass without --no-verify
success_metrics.ats_keywords: Every must-have JD keyword present as the posting's literal string, none more than three times
success_metrics.requirement_coverage: Every required hard skill on the page, evidenced in a bullet or listed in a Technical Skills row; only the exclusion-list classes (credentials, degrees, years, languages, work authorisation, soft competencies) are reported as unmet
success_metrics.factual_accuracy: Every company, date, location and credential verified against the input/master-resume-*.md track files
success_metrics.emphasis: Zero inline bold outside technical-skill labels
success_metrics.production_ready: Ready for actual job submission with no manual cleanup
success_metrics.claim_boundary: No rules.unevidenced or absorbed value in a bullet, a Key Projects line, a Tech Stacks line, the summary or the cover letter

constraints: Never fabricate experience, dates, job titles, certifications or metrics
Never generate a certification, and never emit an AI-generated marker
Never write a metric that is not verbatim in a Measured results line in input/projects.md
Never build an experience bullet around a skill that appears in no project Skills used line
Never leave a bracketed placeholder in the deliverable; omit the entry and report the gap in chat
Never claim a JD-only skill: it may be listed in a Technical Skills row, and never written into a bullet, a Key Projects line, a Tech Stacks line, the summary or the cover letter
Never absorb a skill the posting does not name, and never absorb a credential, a degree, a years-of-experience requirement, a spoken language, work authorisation or a soft competency
Never stop to ask the user mid-run; log the uncertainty to data/{slug}/ and finish the deliverable
Facts always come from input/profile.md, the single source; never from a track file
Never satisfy the frozen-facts gate by editing a track file; correct input/profile.md instead
Never select a track absent from input/track-map.json; its 'tracks' object is authoritative for which master-resume-*.md files exist
Match track-map.json terms on word boundaries, never as bare substrings
Never read input/master-resume-bone.md; it is the anonymised sharing template
A fact the user volunteers is written to every input/master-resume-*.md file that carries that section, never to just one
No em dashes, arrows, emoji or AI-register phrasing
No inline bold outside technical-skill labels
Report unmet requirements every run rather than narrowing the keyword list until it scores 100%
Never read another slug's jd-*.txt, even when the expected one is missing
Never reconcile Section 4 behavioural examples across tracks; they differ by design

research_basis.ats_evolution: Modern ATS use ML for contextual relevance scoring
research_basis.quantified_metrics: Numbers parse as structured data and score higher
research_basis.keyword_strategy: Natural integration (1-3x) works better than stuffing
research_basis.keyword_emphasis: Bolding is invisible to ATS and costs human readability when overused, so it is not used
research_basis.formatting: Single serif typeface, greyscale, plain text, no tables or graphics, optimal for parsing
research_basis.length: Two pages is the practical ceiling for recruiter review at this experience level

example_workflow.step1: Pick a run slug and put the posting in input/jd-{slug}.txt. The track resumes are already in place
example_workflow.step2: Run the skill with that slug, e.g. /resume-jd-optimizer hiringcafe. It does not stop to ask anything
example_workflow.step3: Skill picks the matching master-resume-{track}.md files from the JD role responsibilities and ranks them, then reads input/profile.md for the facts and input/projects.md for the projects and metrics
example_workflow.step4: Skill writes the resume and cover letter to output/{YYYYMMDD}/{company}-{position}/
example_workflow.step5: Skill appends anything new or missing to data/{slug}/new-skills.md and data/{slug}/master-resume-gaps.md
example_workflow.step6: Review the chat report, especially 'Not claimed' and 'Omitted for missing detail'
example_workflow.step8: At the weekend, work through the two data/{slug}/ files and fold real skills into the track resumes

supportingFiles.description: Full renderer semantics and the hard limits enforced by verify_resume.py. Read once before the first output write if the inline contract is unclear
Human-voice rules, the banned phrase list, literal keyword coverage, and the Step 10 quiz answer format. Read when writing prose or when the human-style gate fails
Step 8 only: new-skills and gaps entry formats, the single-Grep classification pass, and the master resume sync rules
Unusual conditions only. Not read on a normal run

skills.name: Resume Project Deepener
skills.description: Expands input/projects.md to the full scope of what a senior engineer actually did on each project, by proposing the unrecorded surface layer by layer and writing only what the candidate confirms, then promoting newly evidenced skills out of rules.unevidenced so bullets may claim them.
skills.author: Resume Generator Team

supporting_files.scope-inventory.md: The senior-scope catalogue: what a project like this one plausibly touched, layer by layer, with the question that would evidence each item. A question generator, never a fact source.

phases: Step 1: Back up input/projects.md, then read the record and the gaps logs
Step 2: Rank the gaps by what a confirmation would buy on the page
Step 3: Derive the unrecorded scope per project from scope-inventory.md
Step 4: Ask in batches of at most 8, answerable in a few words
Step 5: Write only confirmed answers, preserving the entry contract
Step 6: Run scripts/promote_skills.py for whatever the record now evidences
Step 7: Report what was added, promoted and left unconfirmed

success_metrics.provenance: Every line written traces to an explicit confirmation in the conversation
success_metrics.metrics: No figure in Measured results that the candidate did not state
success_metrics.reversibility: A dated backup of input/projects.md exists before the first write
success_metrics.promotion: Skills the record now evidences are out of rules.unevidenced and claimable in bullets

constraints: Nothing reaches input/projects.md without an explicit confirmation; proposals stage in data/proposals/
Never invent a metric, and never round, annualise or convert one the candidate stated
Never add a technology the candidate did not name, whatever a posting asks for
Never widen an answer beyond the project it was given about
Never phrase a question to invite a yes
Never edit input/profile.md facts or input/master-resume-bone.md
An asked-and-skipped item is staged and dropped, not asked again next session
